results.title: Decoding Technical Diagrams: A Survey of AI Methods for Image ...
results.content: Studies were considered eligible for inclusion if they met the following criteria: (1) published between January 2020 and August 2025; (2) proposed, implemented, or evaluated methods for technical diagram extraction or understanding that process complete diagram images to extract structural, semantic, or relational information at the diagram level rather than addressing individual symbols or text elements in isolation; (3) written in English; and (4) provided sufficient methodological detail, including model architecture, training setup, and datasets, to support assessment of transparency and reproducibility. From each eligible study, the following data elements were systematically extracted: author(s), publication year, deep learning architecture type (e.g., CNN, RNN/LSTM, transformer, graph neural network), target diagram type(s) (e.g., flowchart, block and UML diagram, electrical schematic, timing diagram), diagram analysis task(s) addressed (e.g., detection, segmentation, symbol recognition, text extraction, structural parsing, relationship inference, or end-to-end interpretation), dataset characteristics (synthetic versus real-world diagrams, publicly available versus proprietary datasets), and performance metrics.

results.content: Big Data, Network Sciences, and Machine Learning have fundamentally challenged the basic characterizations in computing, from the conventional graph-theoretical modeling of networks to the traditional polynomial-time worst-case measures of efficiency:. This workshop will provide a venue for both the research and engineering communities to discuss and formulate the challenges, utilize opportunities, and propose new ideas in the practice and theory of deep learning on high-dimensional, sparse and imbalanced data. This workshop is a forum for exchanging ideas and methods for mining and learning with graphs, developing new common understandings of the problems at hand, sharing of data sets where applicable, and leveraging existing knowledge from different disciplines. The goals of this workshop are to: (1) highlight the significant challenges that underpin learning and mining from time series data (e.g. irregular sampling, spatiotemporal structure, uncertainty quantification), (2) discuss recent algorithmic, theoretical, statistical, or systems-based developments for tackling these problems, and (3) exploring new frontiers in time series analysis and their connections with important topics such as knowledge representation, reasoning, control, and business intelligence.

results.title: Publications Archives - SIGDA
results.content: This highlights the pressing need for electronic-photonic design automation (EPDA) tools that can streamline the physical design of modern PICs. In this paper, *for the first time*, we propose an open-source automated PIC detailed routing tool, dubbed LiDAR, to generate DRV-free PIC layout for large-scale real-world PICs. LiDAR features a grid-based curvy-aware A\* engine with adaptive crossing insertion, congestion-aware net ordering and objective, and crossing-waveguide optimization scheme, all tailored to the unique property of PIC. Since existing simulation methods are computationally intensive and time-consuming, we propose a graph attention network-based (GAT-based) framework, with novel aggregation methods in the GAT models and informative fine-grained graph generation methods, to achieve efficient analysis of current crowding and IR drops in face-to-face 3D IC TSVs. For current density and voltage predictions, the proposed framework attains R2 scores of 0.9776 and 0.9952 compared to ground truth results, respectively.
